chunks: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him),
'(What about) the eggs in the thickets?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever has equal ends — do not eat it; and whatever has different ends — eat it.'

key_terms.اخْتَلَفَ: differs, unequal ends — characteristic of bird eggs (which are permissible)
key_terms.اسْتَوَى: equal, rounded on both ends — characteristic of reptile eggs (which are forbidden)
key_terms.الْآجَام: thickets, reed beds, dense vegetation near water — common habitat for wild birds and reptiles
key_terms.طَرَفَاهُ: its two ends — the distinguishing feature used to classify eggs

ai.seo_question: How do you identify which eggs are halal to eat according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Zurara asks Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) about identifying which eggs found in the wild are permissible to eat. The Imam provides a practical physical criterion: eggs with two equal/rounded ends (like those of reptiles) are forbidden, while eggs with two unequal ends (one pointed and one rounded, like bird eggs) are permissible. This ruling addresses the practical challenge of identifying permissible eggs from unknown animals in natural settings such as reed beds and thickets.
